blocks.text: HOT TUB REMOVAL FAQ
Hot Tub Removal in Pickering — What to Know Before You Book

items.q: How much does hot tub removal cost in Pickering?
a: Pricing is confirmed on site once the crew sees the tub’s size, condition and how hard it is to get to — a portable spa costs less than a full six-seater with tight gate access. The number covers draining, cutting, hauling and disposal together, with per-unit pricing available if a builder needs several removals across a project.

items.q: Our hot tub hasn't been used in twenty years — is that a problem?
a: Yes — it’s regular work for us in Vaughan. Removal books against your project’s sequence like any other trade, with a committed date that holds, and per-project pricing for builders and renovation companies clearing more than one property.

items.q: Do I need to drain the hot tub myself before you arrive?
a: No — draining is part of the service. The Live Junk Free crew handles it safely on arrival, and you don’t need a hose, a pump, or any prep beyond making sure the area around the tub is reasonably accessible.

items.q: Is it safe to remove a hot tub that's still wired to electrical?
a: Only once the power is confirmed off. If your tub has a hardwired 240V connection, we ask that a licensed electrician disconnect it before the crew arrives — we don’t disconnect live electrical ourselves, for your safety and ours.

items.q: Can you clear an old hot tub from a lot we just bought in Seaton?
a: Yes — this is regular work for us as new lots change hands. The old tub clears ahead of your landscaping or construction schedule, at the same flat pricing as anywhere else in the city.

items.q: Will removing the hot tub damage my deck?
a: It shouldn’t, if it’s done right. Live Junk Free cuts the tub into sections small enough to clear the gate or deck opening rather than dragging or forcing the whole unit through, and protects deck boards and patios along the removal path.
